notes.itemTitle: Pay EUR 53,000 tuition instalment
notes.title: Thursday is the tuition date
notes.text: You dated the EUR 53,000 instalment 5 November, and the SBI sanction task is not dated until the 10th, so the money has to come from somewhere else first. You also fly to India on the 4th, the day before. - Worth starting the transfer this weekend rather than in transit.

notes.itemTitle: Close the KITAS and withdraw BPJS
notes.title: The KITAS closes before you fly
notes.text: Closing the KITAS and withdrawing BPJS is dated 8 November, but you leave Indonesia on the 4th and the exit permit has to be done before the expiry, not after. You are still waiting on InCorp's revised quote. - Worth chasing them now, since the window closes when you fly.

notes.itemTitle: Work through the LMS tutorials
notes.title: Two new LMS tiles Wednesday
notes.text: Pre-Programme Newsletter #9 says you will be enrolled in two more tiles by Wednesday. The Student Life one carries the immigration, visa and medical insurance material and the Fontainebleau guide. - Worth opening the LMS before you fly, since that is the day it lands.

notes.itemTitle: Apply: Amazon Launch MBA intern, Luxembourg
notes.title: Amazon session is tomorrow
notes.text: Amazon's info session on Pathways and Launch is tomorrow, and INSEAD says to apply straight after because the roles fill on a rolling basis. Your Launch application is dated the 8th and you fly on Wednesday. - Worth doing the application the same evening as the session.

notes.itemTitle: Work through the LMS tutorials
notes.title: LMS, a week late
notes.text: A week past its date now, and the weekend I pointed you at has gone. Wednesday is your flight, Thursday is the PLDP webinar, and the assignments it explains start the day after. This is the last time I raise it - the task stays on the board either way.

notes.itemTitle: Submit the visa application at VFS New Delhi
notes.title: Delhi's reply window
notes.text: Your question about the VFS steps reached Muskan Jain and Shubhra Sharma. The out of office is from their manager Shagun Handa, back on 16 November, so it needs no chasing. Delhi asks for two to three working days at this time of year, so expect an answer mid-week while you are travelling.

notes.itemTitle: Decide on Business Foundations and register
notes.title: Business Foundations is done
notes.body: You registered on 26 October, paid the 1,530 euro fee on the 30th, and INSEAD Finance confirmed receipt this morning. The board still had this open as an undecided question, which was wrong. - Closed it on the strength of those emails; the module itself stays on the calendar for 16 to 20 November.

notes.title: Tuition is Thursday
notes.text: Thursday is the date and you fly Wednesday, so tomorrow is the last clear day to start it. Nothing on the board says the transfer has gone. - If it has, mark it paid and it drops off this list.

notes.itemTitle: Close the KITAS and withdraw BPJS
notes.title: Two days left in country
notes.text: The cancellation and the exit permit have to be done from Indonesia, and you leave on Wednesday. The task is dated the 8th, which is the expiry, not the last day you can act on it. - Worth calling InCorp tomorrow rather than waiting on the quote by email.

notes.itemTitle: Amazon Launch online assessment
notes.title: Assessment is the last step
notes.body: Your Amazon Launch application is in, six days early. One required step is left: the online assessment, which expires 2 December. Amazon will not review the application until it is done. - Give it one uninterrupted sitting rather than squeezing it between other things.

notes.text: Chitra at InCorp wrote overnight that a renewal is no longer possible, because it had to start a month before the 8 November expiry. notes.itemTitle: Apply: Google Business Analyst MBA intern, Dublin
notes.title: Google closes while you travel
notes.text: Today is the start-by for both Google applications, Dublin and London, and they close on the 8th while you are moving countries. The Amazon one is in, so the CV is ready to reuse. - Worth doing both today while you are still at a desk.

notes.itemTitle: Amazon Launch online assessment
notes.title: Two hours, within the week
notes.text: Amazon's assessment mail says to complete it within the week, and that you do not move forward without it. It asks for at least two uninterrupted hours on a laptop with a solid connection. - Worth doing today, because the week runs out while you are moving to India.

notes.itemTitle: Amazon Launch online assessment
notes.title: Assessment still open
notes.text: The assessment is dated today and the board shows nothing moved on it. Amazon wants two uninterrupted hours and will not take the application further without it, and tomorrow you are flying. - Tonight is the last quiet two hours you have for a while.

notes.itemTitle: Close the KITAS and withdraw BPJS
notes.title: You are out of Indonesia
notes.text: You told Chitra today that you left Indonesia yesterday and will work online until 6 December, so the departure step is done. What your mail does not say is whether the KITAS cancellation itself was completed before you flew. - Worth asking InCorp to confirm that in writing, because the expiry is the 8th.

notes.itemTitle: Amazon Launch online assessment
notes.title: First come, first served
notes.text: INSEAD's recap of Monday's Amazon session says roles stay open only until the pool is full, and that recruiters interview as applications arrive. The assessment mixes practical examples with theory, and they say to prepare against the Leadership Principles. - There is no deadline to wait for, so the assessment is the only thing holding your place in the queue.

notes.itemTitle: Pay EUR 53,000 tuition instalment

notes.text: The 53,000 euro instalment is dated today and the board still shows it open. The SBI sanction is not due until the 10th, so if this one is yours to fund it has to come from your own account. - Last nudge on this one; mark it paid and it drops off.

notes.itemTitle: Pay EUR 53,000 tuition instalment

notes.text: Marie Rose replied this morning that INSEAD cannot confirm in writing that a refund would go back to SBI if your visa is refused. kb.label: IAA Alumni Meet & Greet
kb.body: The INSEAD Alumni Association's own introduction to the network: who they are, what the regional chapters do, and how alumni actually get used during and after the MBA. Optional in INSEAD's own rating, and the one P0 session that is about the twenty years after the degree rather than the year of it.

kb.label: PLDP intro webinar
kb.body: On Zoom. Walks through the Personal Leadership Development Programme: what the P0 assignments ask for, how individual and group coaching fit together across the year, and what your coach does with what you write. INSEAD marks this MUST DO, and it is the session that makes the assignment window make sense rather than feel like homework.

kb.label: AMA on student platforms
kb.body: An open question session on the tools you are about to live in: the LMS, CareerGlobe, and the rest of the stack. Optional, and worth it only if something in the platforms is already confusing you by then.

kb.label: INSEAD CV & Cover Letter webinar
kb.body: 13:00 Paris / 20:00 Singapore. What belongs in the INSEAD CV format and what gets cut, how recruiters read it, and where the CV work sits in the year: a first draft through VMock before a human sees it, then review with your coach, and the CV Book after that. Must-do for career switchers.

kb.label: Academics overview webinar
kb.body: On Zoom, with the MBA Programme Management Director and current students. The curriculum end to end, how the core and electives fit, exemptions, and what people wish they had done before arriving. Highly recommended rather than required, and the one place to ask a second-hand question about workload.

kb.label: Your Summer Experience & Prep for Arrival
kb.body: The three honest ways to spend the eight-week break after P3: a short-term summer project with a company, a startup tour, or deliberate time off to prepare for full-time recruitment. Also covers arrival logistics. This is the session that decides what you spend P2 recruiting for.

kb.label: Business Foundations: register by 30 October
kb.body: The course itself runs one week online, 16-20 November: an intensive introduction to Financial Accounting, Finance and Quantitative Methods aimed at people arriving without a quant background. Optional, registered through MyINSEAD, and the decision has to be made three weeks before it runs.

kb.label: CareerLeader and Career Anchors, before the first coaching session
kb.body: Two profiling questionnaires plus the workbook questions that go with them. They are the entire raw material for the first coaching conversation, so the session is only as good as what you put in: arriving without them turns a 45-minute slot into an introduction you could have had by email. The CDC's mail of 12 October carries the mechanism: register at careerleader.com as a new user with your INSEAD address and the registration key that mail holds — the key is deliberately not recorded here, because this repository is public — then complete the profile and the three assessments and keep the report for the session. Career Anchors is an Excel workbook downloaded from INSEAD's own site. Thirty minutes and twenty, so both fit in one evening. Coaching slots open in early November.

kb.label: PLDP assignments window
kb.body: Delivered online through the LMS across roughly seven weeks. Your coach reads these before meeting you, so they are what shapes the coaching you get rather than a box to tick. INSEAD marks them MUST DO, and the window deliberately spans the December break because they are not a single sitting.

kb.label: Launch Week career pre-work appears on the LMS
kb.body: Posted in early December, to be completed before Launch Week rather than during it. Launch Week is dense enough that anything left undone gets done badly or not at all, and the career workshop assumes the pre-work is behind you.

kb.label: P0, the pre-programme period
kb.body: Where the board is right now: the twelve weeks between the LMS going live and Launch Week. Three strands run through it at once -- Academics, Careers and Student Life -- and almost everything in the Webinars and Deadlines blocks sits inside this stretch. It ends the day Launch Week begins.

kb.label: Launch Week
kb.body: Fontainebleau, eleven days. The P1 core exemption exams sit inside it along with orientation, the career workshop and the first run of sessions that set up P1. The pre-work that goes with it lands on the LMS in early December.

kb.label: Period dates, P1 to P5
kb.body: Five eight-week periods across eleven months, with a long summer gap in the middle. INSEAD publishes these as provisional and says they can still move, so treat anything booked around the edges as provisional too.

kb.label: Breaks
kb.body: Three short ones and the long summer. The short breaks are not empty: career treks and club treks run in them, which is most of what people mean when they say the MBA has no holidays. The 1 July to 22 August gap is the one the summer project fits inside.

kb.label: Campus exchange bidding happens during P1
kb.body: Campus is Fontainebleau or Singapore for P1 and P2; exchange opens from P3 onwards, and the bidding for it runs inside P1 while you are still finding your feet. The rules change year to year, so the P1 briefing is the authority rather than anything written now.

kb.label: Graduation, Singapore
kb.body: Singapore campus, with the grad trip after it. Twenty-three months from the deposit to the gown.

kb.label: LMS
kb.body: Live from 26 October. Every piece of academic content runs through it, a chunk of the CDC curriculum as well, and club registration too. The PLDP assignments are delivered here.

kb.label: CareerGlobe
kb.body: Live from 27 October. The CDC platform: appointments, jobs, events. The profile has to be set up before you can book the first coaching appointment, which makes it the gate on everything else CDC.

kb.label: VMock
kb.body: Part 1 of the INSEAD CV process. It scores a draft against the format and tells you what to fix, so the version a human finally reads is not the first one you wrote.

kb.label: The INSEAD CV format
kb.body: One format, used as a networking and marketing document rather than a record of employment, and the basis for the INSEAD CV Book that goes to recruiters. The process runs on through P1, so the first version is not the last.

kb.label: Two teams behind you: a Career Coach and Employer Engagement
kb.body: That is the whole of CDC's structure, and it is worth knowing which one to ask. The coach is your primary contact for strategy, materials and accountability. Employer Engagement are the sector specialists who know what a given industry is actually hiring for this year.

kb.label: Coaching sessions are 45 minutes and you set the agenda
kb.body: Short enough to fit before class, which is deliberate. You bring the update and the question and agree the next steps; the coach pressure-tests the plan rather than making it. A session you arrive at without having done the last set of next steps is a session spent recapping.

kb.label: Your coach is allocated on P1 location and never changes
kb.body: Deliberately coach-agnostic: they are allocated by where you start, follow you the whole MBA including exchange, and there are no coach changes. So the relationship is worth investing in early rather than shopping around.

kb.label: First coaching session, from November
kb.body: Covers how the partnership works, what CareerLeader and Career Anchors said about you, and the three stages of the career journey. CareerGlobe has to be set up before you can book it.

kb.label: The career journey is three stages
kb.body: Self Awareness: strengths, interests, values, and what you actually bring. Market Exploration: industry knowledge built through networking, narrowed to two or three target plans rather than one bet or ten. Execution: a value proposition you can say out loud, and recruiting to each sector's real timetable, which differs by months.

kb.label: Career switcher status decides how much of CDC is must-do
kb.body: Most CDC items are marked must-do for people switching Location, Sector or Function, and only highly recommended for everyone else. Which of the three you are switching is therefore the single input that sets your CDC workload, and it is worth writing down early.

kb.label: Employer Engagement are Sector Advisors
kb.body: Subject-matter experts who split their time between advising students and talking to companies, which is what makes their market read current. They give market intelligence, name who to connect with, sharpen a pitch for a specific sector, and help with offer negotiation.

kb.label: Careers Across Geographies & Sectors workshop
kb.body: February 2027, for Fontainebleau and Singapore. CDC asks 27Ds not to book Sector Advisor appointments until after it, because most of the sector information is delivered there and a one-to-one before it just repeats the workshop. The one exception is roles with early internship application deadlines.

kb.label: Company events, treks and the Industry Expert Series
kb.body: Pre-MBA company event invitations arrive through the Sunday newsletters, which is the practical reason to read them. During the year there are treks, networking forums, the Tech Symposium and the Industry Expert Series.

kb.label: CDC's own key takeaways
kb.body: Networking is what works: alumni first, then people in the target industry, then classmates. Pick a few priorities rather than defaulting to consulting because it recruits loudest. Take a leadership role in a club. A radical career changer should start before the programme, not in P1. If you are targeting one country with no experience there, explore widely early and aim at roles where local competition is thinner. And only apply where you genuinely fit, because the interview exposes the rest.

kb.label: PLDP runs the whole year, not just P0
kb.body: The Personal Leadership Development Programme: individual and group coaching that starts with the P0 assignments and continues across the periods. It is the leadership counterpart to CDC's career coaching, and it is the one INSEAD flags as high-importance alongside CDC.

kb.label: Internship recruiting runs through P2
kb.body: March to May 2027. Some internships start as early as June, before P3 finishes. Roles with early application deadlines are the one reason to approach Employer Engagement before the February workshop.

kb.label: The summer project itself: optional, 8 weeks
kb.body: A Short-Term Summer Project in the break after P3. The alternatives INSEAD names are a startup tour or deliberate time off to prepare for full-time recruitment, and it does not treat the internship as obligatory for this cohort. Gavin's own plan is to start looking from the day the course starts rather than waiting for P2.

kb.label: Six P1 core courses
kb.body: Financial Accounting, Financial Markets & Valuation, Organisational Behaviour I, Prices & Markets, Uncertainty Data & Judgment, and Introduction to Strategy. Three of the six are quantitative, which is what Business Foundations exists for.

kb.label: P1 pre-readings
kb.body: For Financial Accounting and Prices & Markets specifically, with book recommendations on the MBA Journey pages. Highly recommended rather than required, which in practice means the people who do them have an easier first three weeks.

kb.label: Core exemption exams
kb.body: P1 core exemptions are examined during Launch Week; P2 and P3 exemptions are taken during P1. Passing one frees the slot for an elective, so an exemption is worth a course you would rather take than a week of revision saved.

kb.label: Club introduction and registration
kb.body: Runs through the LMS from 26 October. Club leadership elections and the handover to the 27D cohort come in P1 and P2, so the clubs you join now are the ones you can take a leadership role in later, which CDC names as one of its key takeaways.

kb.label: 27D Student Council and Student Rep elections
kb.body: January 2027. Team diversity is a stated requirement for the slates, so the teams form before the election rather than after it.

kb.label: Programme questions
kb.body: degree.programmes@insead.edu for anything about the programme itself: dates, registration, admin, documents.

kb.label: Career questions
kb.body: careerdevelopmentcentre@insead.edu for CDC: coaching, CareerGlobe, Employer Engagement, anything career.

kb.label: Career Coach
kb.body: Your primary contact all year. Career strategy, target and transferable skills, networking approach, CV and cover letter review, elevator pitch, mock interviews, choosing between offers, and holding you accountable.

kb.label: MBA-Exchange.com
kb.body: The CDC's third-party global careers platform, premium access through INSEAD's partnership: vetted postings, industry and country reports, employer profiles with Talent Radar visibility, and Talent Talks with recruiters. The welcome mail arrived on 5 October with a login of your INSEAD address and a password in plain text, so change that password on first login — the password itself is deliberately not recorded here, because this repository is public. Bilal Ojjeh, their founder, offers himself as the direct contact.

kb.label: Aced, formerly Exponent
kb.body: Technical interview preparation, free through an INSEAD invitation that landed on 5 October: courses in software engineering, SQL and data analytics and system design, mock technical interviews, a question bank of recently asked questions, and company-by-company hiring guides. Sign up at aced.io with the INSEAD address the invitation was sent to. It is the one career platform aimed at technical interviews rather than the consulting-and-finance case track that CaseCoach covers.

kb.label: CaseCoach
kb.body: Case interview preparation, free on the INSEAD subscription, which you registered for on 5 October. Their own course opens with what to expect from a case interview and is reading rather than a task; the founder, Enguerran Loos, is a former consultant and headhunter for the top three firms. It is the consulting-and-finance counterpart to Aced's technical track, and the one to work through if consulting stays on your list.

kb.label: Why the pre-MBA window had already closed
kb.body: McKinsey's Make Your Mark, BCG Unlock and Bain's ExperienceBain are all aimed at people who have been admitted and have not started yet, and they run over the northern summer: registration falls roughly May to July, the programme itself August to December. That is built around an autumn intake. The January 2027 intake's equivalent window had passed before the admission letter arrived, which is why Make Your Mark was never a thing that could have been applied to from here. Nothing was missed through not looking; the calendar simply does not line up. What replaces it is the on-campus cycle, which starts in P1.

kb.label: McKinsey Make Your Mark
kb.body: A pre-MBA mentorship programme for incoming MBA students at a named set of schools, INSEAD among them: one-to-one mentoring with a McKinsey consultant, recruiting workshops, networking and interview coaching, running from late August to the end of December. Applications have closed in July in recent cycles. It is a mentorship and a foot in the door rather than an offer, and the thing it actually buys is knowing how the firm recruits before everyone else does.

kb.label: BCG Unlock
kb.body: BCG's pre-MBA virtual event series: sessions with BCG leaders and consultants on what consulting work is, plus skill-building and networking, over the summer before the programme starts. Registration has been encouraged by mid-May and then reviewed on a rolling basis after that. Virtual, so geography is not the constraint - the admission timing is.

kb.label: ExperienceBain
kb.body: Bain's virtual pre-MBA programme for incoming first-years at eligible schools: interactive sessions with Bain teams around the world across the summer, flexible rather than a fixed week. Recent cycles have closed applications in early May. Same shape and the same timing problem as the other two.

kb.label: Amazon Pathways (MBA Operations LDP)
kb.body: Amazon's three-year operations leadership development programme, open to people enrolled in an MBA or within 24 months of graduating, with cohorts tied to a start year rather than a single deadline. There is no closing date at all: applications are read on a rolling basis and the posting comes down when they have enough people, which makes early the whole strategy. It is the closest fit on the Big Tech list to five years of SaaS presales and operations - a management track rather than a functional hire.

kb.label: How the Big Tech and consumer cycles are timed
kb.body: Both run on graduation year, not on intake. The 2027 postings at Amazon, J&J and their peers say "graduating between August 2026 and August 2027", which a December 2027 graduation sits outside - so the cycle that matters is the one that opens in autumn 2027, and anything open now is worth applying to only where the eligibility text actually admits it. The practical consequence: the autumn 2027 window is the one to be ready for, and the preparation for it (CV, CareerGlobe, the CDC coach) is already on the board.

kb.label: What the Sunday brief watches
kb.body: Every Sunday the weekly report carries a NEWS section: pre-MBA and in-programme opportunities researched against the three target groups - Big Tech LDP and management-track roles, MBB consulting, and consumer LDPs. Anything worth doing becomes a task titled [NEWS], drawn in magenta, with Accept and Reject on its card. A week with nothing says so rather than padding. This group is where the findings that are facts rather than tasks collect.

kb.label: The French APS is France-only, and it is the thing that removes sponsorship
kb.body: Graduating at Fontainebleau makes him a French master's graduate, which entitles him to the APS (autorisation provisoire de sejour, also called the RECE) -- a residence permit that lets him work in France without an employer sponsoring anything. That is the answer to the barrier he hit when job-hunting: outside France an employer has to sponsor from scratch, in France it only has to convert a permit he already holds. The permit is national, so it carries no right to work in Germany, Spain or the Netherlands, and the usual quoted length is 12 months with sources disagreeing about a longer window for Indian nationals. Its real value is as a bridge: a year of legal French employment is what makes the next two routes available.

kb.label: How a French job becomes a job anywhere in the EU
kb.body: Two mechanisms, both on a clock that only starts once he is employed. The EU Blue Card is issued for a graduate-level job above a salary threshold, and after roughly twelve months in the first country it allows a move to another EU state on a simplified application rather than a fresh sponsorship. EU long-term residence arrives at five years of legal residence and carries broad mobility with it. So the sequence that actually works is France first on the APS, convert to a Blue Card, then move -- not applying cold into the Netherlands or Spain from outside.

kb.label: The top five cities, ranked -- and why Paris is no longer the base
kb.body: Reranked on 2 November 2026 after he said he does not speak French and has no intention of learning it. That changes what Paris is worth, because the APS only pays off on roles he could actually take in France. 1. Dublin -- the Critical Skills Employment Permit qualifies on salary alone with no labour market test, it works in English, and Google, Meta, Microsoft, Stripe and Workday run EMEA from there; rent and weather are the cost. 2. Amsterdam -- English-language workplaces are normal and it is the best of these to live in, but the zoekjaar probably does not cover an INSEAD degree, so the offer has to come first. 3. Paris -- narrow rather than out. Consulting in France is French-speaking and MBB Paris will not take him for French client work without it; consumer goods is the same at LVMH, Danone and L'Oreal. What survives is Big Tech EMEA offices, which genuinely operate in English, and that happens to be his first-choice industry. 4. Singapore -- an INSEAD campus and a deep alumni base, English, the APAC seat for most Big Tech, a manageable Employment Pass, and the one market where his five years in South-East Asia read as an asset. 5. Barcelona or Madrid -- in on the Spanish he is building and on leisure, out on Big Tech density and pay. Just outside: Brussels, lowest salary bar of the group. Ruled out: Switzerland on the labour market test and quota; Germany, the UK and the UAE by his own choice; Copenhagen is a company target rather than a city target. The consequence that matters more than the order: with the APS usable only on English-speaking tech roles in France, the post-graduation search year is no longer a safety net, so the plan is offer-first and the recruiting has to happen in P1 and P2.

kb.label: A summer internship abroad needs its own permission, and it is not the student visa
kb.body: His French student residence permit covers work in France and nothing outside it, so each of the internship markets has its own route. Ireland uses the Atypical Working Scheme, which must be applied for from outside Ireland and wants at least twelve weeks' notice -- that lead time is the one that bites, since the applications close in November for a July start. Luxembourg requires a trainee authorisation arranged by the host company. The UK route is Temporary Work -- Government Authorised Exchange, again employer-led. The United States is possible rather than closed: the J-1 Intern category explicitly covers students enrolled at a university outside the US, but a State Department designated sponsor has to issue the DS-2019, so it depends entirely on whether the employer already runs that programme. The practical rule is to ask the recruiter which route they use before assuming an offer is workable.

kb.label: The Dutch orientation year, and the ranking rule it turns on
kb.body: The zoekjaar is the Netherlands' post-study search year. It is open to graduates of a Dutch institution, or to graduates of an institution in the top 200 of the accepted rankings -- and the detail that matters is which rankings those are. IND accepts Times Higher Education, QS and ShanghaiRanking/ARWU, counting both their general lists and their by-subject lists where the subject matches what you studied. The QS Global MBA Ranking, where INSEAD places first or second, is a different product and is not one of them. The rule was also tightened: top 200 in at least TWO of the three publishers is now required, not one. INSEAD plausibly appears in QS by subject for Business and Management, but THE and ARWU rank research-and-teaching institutions and a standalone business school typically does not enter them, so one of three is the likely answer and that does not clear the bar. Worth checking rather than assuming, because if two come back yes then Amsterdam is a landing point rather than a second move. Until then the Dutch route runs through an employer and a Blue Card, so the offer has to come first -- which is the whole reason Paris is the base and Amsterdam is not.

kb.label: The 27D job report is the CDC's live list of what is open now
kb.body: A spreadsheet circulated with the newsletter, listing roles open to the 27D cohort with company, title, location, type and deadline. It mixes full-time graduate roles with summer internships and the type column is not always right -- a Google row tagged full-time is titled MBA intern. It is the source the five application tasks on the board came from, and it is reissued, so it is worth re-reading each time rather than treating the current shortlist as final. Deadlines on it run close: four of the five chosen roles close on 8 November.

kb.label: Your internship window starts 1 July, not 24 June
kb.body: INSEAD's P0 recap puts the official 27D summer break at 1 July to 22 August 2027, with classes back on 23 August. In Singapore P3 core and electives both end on 23 June, so students there can start an internship on 24 June; in Fontainebleau P3 core also ends on 23 June but the electives run to 30 June, so his own earliest start is 1 July unless he drops them. The CDC added that tech internships often need longer than the official eight weeks, which is a conversation to have with the employer rather than with the school.

news.body:
## Tomorrow
- Plan Locus exit, due 7 Oct, and the only Critical thing with a date this week.
There is no resignation date, no notice period and no last working day on the board. What last working day are you aiming for, and do you owe notice? The January move hangs off that one date.

## Not yours right now
- Campus France, corrected preconsular file sent yesterday afternoon.
Nothing to do but wait. What it gates: EEF validation reads 21 Oct and the VFS appointment is 10 Nov, so there is about three weeks of slack behind it. If validation slips past the 21st, that slack is gone.
- SBI sanction letter, due 24 Oct.
The PoA was executed at Hindon on 3 Oct, so the bank should have everything. Is anything still outstanding from your side, or is it purely theirs now?

## Worth an hour this week
- VMock and CaseCoach both went live yesterday, good.
The CDC mail that came with them wants CareerLeader and Career Anchors done before your first coaching session, which is why booking the coach still reads as blocked. They are due 31 Oct and take an hour or two. Start with CareerLeader: it is the longer one and it feeds the report the CDC asks for.

## The passport is the decision now
- TLS keeps your passport from the day you submit, now dated 23 October, for two to three weeks.
Three things want it in that window: the exit permit for your KITAS, your flight out of Jakarta, and the visa itself. The ways out are different enough that choosing is the work -- submit before you leave and ask whether someone else can collect, apply from India after you land, or move your departure. Tell me which and I will set every date after it accordingly.
- The 16 October interview still waits on a courier.
Your originals reach you early next week, and Fitria postpones the interview if they are not in your hand on the day. Tracking on that parcel is what would let you confirm the slot rather than hope.

## Nothing here waits on anyone
- Create your France-Visas and TLS Contact accounts.
Fitria asked for both and neither needs the interview done first, so this is the one piece of the visa you can finish today.
- Upload your CV to VMock, 18 October.
The next date on the board that is nobody's but yours, and it is a short job.

## Wednesday's interview is the whole visa now
- Campus France put you at 10:00 on Wednesday 14 October, two days earlier than the board had it.
Fitria gave you the earliest slot you asked for, and the originals still have to be in your hand on the day, so the courier is the only thing standing between you and it. A tracking number today is what turns Wednesday from a hope into a plan.
- Submitting at TLS two working days after the interview, rather than on the 23rd, is what saves your flight.
Fitria put submission about two working days after the interview and a decision about fifteen days after that. From 16 October that lands at the end of the month; from the 23rd it lands on 7 November, the day you leave Jakarta. Creating your France-Visas and TLS Contact accounts this weekend is what lets you book the slot the moment the interview ends.

## The loan has less slack than it looks
- The SBI sanction is dated 24 October and the 5 November instalment sits behind it.
Your branch has not come back since you told them on 6 October that the charges confirmation went on the 3rd. Monday is a working day there, and a call to the branch will move this where another email has not.

## What moved
- You cleared the Campus France file and two of the career platforms.
The EEF was validated and the fee paid on 6 October, the extra documents went on the 5th, and VMock access and Case Coach were both closed the same day. Five tasks closed in the week, all of them yours rather than anyone else's.
- The visa turned out to be three weeks earlier than the board thought.
Campus France refused the interview exemption on Thursday, which revived a task you had deleted, and in the same conversation Fitria put submission at about two working days after the interview. That moved it from 10 November to 23 October, and the provider is TLS Contact, not VFS.
- On Saturday evening you did the unglamorous half.
The France-Visas account, your employer's details for the form, and a request to SBI for an in-principle sanction letter. None of it shows as a tick and all three were holding up the submission.

## What did not
- The SBI branch has not written since 6 October.
Their last substantive word was on 27 September, that verification of the collateral would take more time. Two requests are sitting with them now, not one.
- Your degree originals are still with the courier.
Wednesday's interview needs them in your hand, and nothing on the board says where the parcel is.
- Career did not move at all.
Writing down your post-MBA function, industry and geography is still open, and CareerGlobe, the two questionnaires, the CV and the first CDC session all sit behind it.

## Risks
- The passport window is the one that can cost you the flight.
TLS keeps your passport from submission until the decision, about fifteen days by Fitria's account. Submitting on 16 October gets it back near the end of the month; submitting on the 23rd gets it back around 7 November, the day you leave Jakarta, and you need it for the KITAS exit permit as well. Every day between the interview and the submission comes off that margin.
- Proof of funds has quietly become a visa problem and not only a tuition one.
The loan used to be a 5 November deadline. The visa file now needs evidence of it too, and both requests sit with the same branch that has gone quiet. If the in-principle letter does not come, the submission has nothing to show.
- One parcel gates the whole visa sequence.
The interview, the submission, the decision and the exit permit all run off a courier nobody has a tracking number for.
- The career chain is the cheapest thing to fix and the most expensive to leave.
One question only you can answer unblocks four tasks, and the first CDC coaching session is already dated 15 November.

## Put first this week
- Write back to Fitria and confirm Wednesday. One line, and everything downstream waits on it.
- Call the branch on Monday, and ask for the in-principle letter and the state of the full sanction in the same call.
- Get the tracking number today, so Tuesday is not when you find out the parcel is late.
- Answer the post-MBA question. Nobody outside is holding that one up.

## Two decisions sitting on the board
- Amazon Pathways, the operations LDP, dated 15 November.
It is a rolling posting with no deadline, which comes down when they have enough people, so the date on the board is a prompt rather than theirs. Accept it and it becomes an ordinary task; reject it and it goes.
- The MBB pre-MBA programmes are closed for your intake.
Make Your Mark, BCG Unlock and ExperienceBain all run over the summer for people starting in the autumn, so the January window has gone. The route from here is the on-campus cycle in P1, which is a calendar to pin down rather than an application to chase.

## The nearest date is your CV
- Upload your CV to VMock, 18 October.
Nothing else on the board is dated before it and it is a short job. The score is what tells you what to fix, and the INSEAD CV itself is due 2 November, so doing it this weekend leaves two clear weeks to act on what it says.

## Business Foundations needs an answer before the bank gives you one
- Registration closes 30 October. You are holding it for the SBI sanction, due 24 October.
That is six days of margin on an optional quant primer that runs 16 to 20 November online. If the sanction slips past the 24th, do you register anyway and carry the cost, or let the course go?

## The exit route just changed
- InCorp has offered to cancel the KITAS after you leave
Chitra came back overnight with a 10 percent discount and, more usefully, an ERP cancellation done once you have already flown, instead of an EPO before you go. That is the first option anyone has put forward that does not need your passport in Jakarta while the consulate is holding it. Worth asking her today what ERP requires and whether Locus will sponsor it that way.
## Wednesday needs two things from you
- Where is the courier with your degree certificate?
Fitria needs the originals in your hand on the day, and nothing on the board says where the parcel is. If it is not in Jakarta by Tuesday, telling her on Tuesday is a postponement and telling her on Wednesday morning is a wasted slot.
- She still has not heard back about the 10am slot
She offered Wednesday and nothing has gone back to her. One line confirms it, and you can still move it if the parcel is late.
## Today is the first day the branch is open
- Nobody has had a working day on your in-principle letter yet
You asked for it on Saturday and Indian branches were shut yesterday. Nothing has come back on that thread since you answered their charges question on 6 Oct, and the visa file needs the letter before the 23rd, so a call will be faster than waiting on the reply.

## Tomorrow's interview is the easy half
- The TLS slot becomes bookable the moment it ends.
Fitria put submission about two working days after the interview and the decision about fifteen days after that. Your board still says 23 October, and that is the version where your passport comes back around 7 November, the day you fly. Take the earliest slot TLS offers you, not the one that matches the board.
- Can you still get into TLScontact?
The activation link arrived on Sunday and nothing says you have used it. A login that does not work on Thursday costs exactly the days an early slot was meant to buy.
- Does SBI's in-principle offer need signing before it counts?
It came yesterday with an application form attached, which suggests the letter is not finished business. Proof of funds is a submission document, so it has to be in a form you can hand over this week, not in late October.

## The career track has a November problem
- Your first coaching session opens in the week you move.
The CDC wrote yesterday that coaches take 1:1s from early November, and that CareerLeader and Career Anchors must both be done first. That is the week you leave Jakarta and the week the KITAS expires, so the real window for two assessments worth fifty minutes is the next fortnight.
- Good job on the VMock upload on Sunday, 63 and into the yellow zone.
The SMART Editor is what takes it to green. Writing down your post-MBA function, industry and geography is still what the rest of this track is waiting on.

## This morning, and the four days after it
- Both halves of Wednesday are closed.
You wrote to Fitria yesterday afternoon confirming 10am in person, and the originals are in your hand. Nothing is left to arrange before the room.
- The apostille is dated Saturday and still reads To-do.
Campus France's October correction asked for the original bachelor certificate in colour and the transcript, which are the same papers the courier has just delivered. Fitria is the one person who can say precisely what the consulate wants apostilled and attested - ask her in the room this morning rather than working it out on Thursday.

## Money
- Does the 5 November instalment need the EUR account?
The EUR 53,000 instalment sits on 5 November and the task for opening the account sits on 30 November, after it. If SBI disburses straight to INSEAD the order is harmless; if any of it has to pass through an account of yours, that date is in the wrong place.

## The route changed yesterday, and October has not caught up
- Your dossier can move to Campus France India.
They confirmed it in Jakarta yesterday and you have asked Delhi what they need. That is the passport trap solved: you no longer have to hand your passport over before you fly on 7 November.
- But the board still has you submitting at TLS on 23 October.
If the plan is now India, that date is pointed at the wrong month, and so is everything feeding it - the SBI letter by the 24th and the apostille on Saturday. Which is it, Jakarta this month or Delhi in November? The order of the next three weeks turns on that one answer.

## Yesterday
- Nothing on the board says how the interview went.
It is still open and dated yesterday, so the whole visa track is reading off a step with no outcome recorded. If Fitria asked for anything further, that is the thing worth writing down while it is fresh.

## India is the plan, and three October dates are not
- You made the call yesterday.
You told Fitria you will apply from India and asked her to move the dossier to New Delhi, so the question this brief put to you on Wednesday is closed. The interview is closed too, dated the 14th.
- The apostille is the one step no route makes unnecessary.
It is dated Sunday and still reads To-do, and whichever consulate takes your file will want the same original certificate and transcript. The TLS date on the 23rd and the SBI letter by the 24th can wait for Delhi to answer; this one cannot, because stamping documents takes days you do not get back.

## Waiting on Locus
- Ravi and Jishnu have not answered since Wednesday.
You asked them to approve InCorp's revised quote and nothing has come back, so your KITAS exit is parked on an approval rather than on the paperwork. You fly on 7 November and the KITAS expires on the 8th - tell them that is the window, not a preference.

## Nothing on the visa track is yours this weekend
- Delhi has the question now, not you.
You asked Fitria to move the dossier and asked Delhi what they need from your side. Until one of them answers, the TLS date and the SBI letter are both waiting on somebody else, which makes this the first free weekend you have had in three.

## The career block is a weekend's work, and it gates November
- Your first CDC coaching session is blocked by two things you could finish today.
CareerGlobe on the 27th and the two questionnaires on the 31st both gate the coaching session dated 15 November, and none of the three has started.
- CareerLeader and Career Anchors are about fifty minutes together.
The CDC's own instructions put them at thirty and twenty minutes, and neither needs an office, a courier or a reply from anyone. They also hand you the vocabulary for the post-MBA statement, which is dated the 31st with nothing written down yet.

## What moved
- You sat the Campus France interview on the 14th and then changed the route.
In person in Jakarta with the originals in hand, after a week of arranging it. Two days later you wrote to Fitria choosing India and asking her to move the dossier to New Delhi. That is the biggest decision on this board since the admission, and you made it in two days.
- Your CV went from 63 to 92.
You uploaded to VMock on the 11th, it came back yellow, and yesterday it came back green with two CDC people copied. That was the one thing this week nobody else could do for you.
- SBI moved from To do to In progress.
The branch sent the in-principle offer and the application form on the 12th.
- You put the KITAS exit to Locus on the 14th.
Ravi and Jishnu were asked to approve InCorp's revised quote.

## What did not
- The apostille was dated yesterday and has not started.
- Nothing from Campus France New Delhi since you wrote on the 14th.
- Nothing on the board says SBI's application form has gone back.
- CareerGlobe, the two CDC questionnaires and the post-MBA statement are all untouched, and all three fall in the last week of October.

## Risks
- Every October date on the visa track is now a guess.
The board still says TLS on the 23rd and the SBI letter by the 24th, and both were built for a Jakarta submission you have abandoned. The real deadlines are your flight on 7 November and the programme on 3 January, and nothing between them is known until Delhi answers. Four days of silence is not alarming yet; four more would be.
- Nobody has asked whether India means sitting the interview again.
It is one sentence in an email and it is the difference between the India route costing days and costing weeks. Your mother's draft letter asked it; none of your own messages has.
- The loan and the tuition are coupled and the coupling is untested.
EUR 53,000 falls on 5 November, the sanction is dated the 24th and is still only in principle, and the task for opening the EUR account sits on 30 November, after the payment. INSEAD extended this instalment once already for exactly this reason.
- The KITAS exit is parked on two colleagues.
You fly on the 7th and it expires on the 8th, so there is no version of this that survives being settled in the first week of November.

## Put first this week
1. One email to Delhi, chasing the transfer and asking the re-interview question in the same breath. Everything else on the visa track is waiting behind that reply.
2. Give Ravi and Jishnu a date rather than a request. The constraint is a flight, not a preference.
3. CareerGlobe and the two questionnaires. The CDC times them at fifty minutes together, they unblock the November coaching session, and they are the only things on this list that nobody else controls.

## The internship applications are what this week is for
- Four applications close on 8 November, the day after you fly.
Google Strategy and Operations in London, Google Business Analyst and Finance in Dublin, and Amazon Launch in Luxembourg all shut on the same day, which falls in your first week in India and the day your KITAS runs out. Four applications on a moving week is how one of them quietly gets dropped.
- The CDC's CV review slots are Thursday, Friday and next Monday.
22, 23 and 26 October, by sector, and they ask for a VMock-formatted CV, which you have at 92 since Saturday. Booking one this week is the difference between four applications and four good ones.

## SBI has a date on Saturday
- Nothing on the board says the application form went back.
The branch sent the in-principle offer and the form on 12 October, and the sanction is dated this Saturday. The 53,000 euro instalment on 5 November is sitting behind it. - If the form has gone, close the loop here; if not, it is this week's one piece of paper.

## The tuition and the loan have stopped lining up
- The sanction is now dated five days after the payment.
Yesterday the SBI task moved to 10 November, because the documents have to be signed at your Indian branch and you only land on the 7th. The 53,000 euro instalment falls on the 5th. INSEAD already moved that date once at your request when the loan was slow, so the question is whether you pay it from your own funds or ask them again - and asking is easier three weeks out than three days out.

## Campus France put the sequence in writing
- Jakarta transfers only after Delhi says yes.
Fitria answered yesterday that she will move the dossier once Campus France New Delhi confirms they will take it, and she wants to be copied on your email to them. That makes Friday's TLS date on the board a date nothing will happen on, and your flight on 7 November the one that counts.

## Four dates in the next ten days, and none of them has started
- The LMS tutorials, CareerGlobe and the two CDC questionnaires are all yours alone.
They fall on the 26th, the 27th and the 31st, every one of them still reads To-do, and together they are about a day's work with nobody else in the way. The questionnaires are also what unblocks your first CDC coaching session, which is dated 15 November.
- The post-MBA statement on the 31st is the one that is actually hard.
Function, industry and geography, written down in one place. The mind map already holds your target countries and the work-rights reasoning behind them, so the thinking exists - what is missing is the page. It decides your electives, your exchange and when you recruit, so it is worth an evening rather than a gap between other things.

## InCorp is waiting on one word from you
- Chitra asked yesterday whether you are renewing or cancelling the KITAS.
She also pointed out that a renewal normally has to start a month before expiry, and 8 November is too close for that now, so the only live question is whether to confirm the cancellation, NPWP revocation and BPJS package she quoted. That quotation has sat unanswered since 12 October, and your BPJS claim goes through the same people. - One line confirming cancellation unblocks all of it.

## Campus France is Delhi's to answer now
- You wrote to New Delhi yesterday and copied Fitria, which is exactly what the transfer was waiting on.
Nothing else on this track is yours until they reply. The task still says TLS Contact tomorrow, and that is a date and a city that cannot happen now you are applying from Delhi after 4 November. - Give it a date you expect to use, or clear it, so it stops sitting in your next ten days.

## CareerGlobe is the only thing left in the way
- You closed the CareerLeader and Career Anchors questionnaires on 18 October.
They were one of the two things holding up your first CDC coaching session. The other is the CareerGlobe profile, dated the 27th and about an hour's work, and once it is done the 15 November booking is yours to make whenever you want it.

## Monday is the last CV review slot
- The CDC is running three, on the 22nd, 23rd and 26th, and today's is the second.
Monday is also the day your LMS tutorials are due, and the Google and Amazon applications close on 8 November. Your VMock CV has been in the green since the 11th, so the review is the last step between that score and four applications. - If Monday is the slot you take, move the LMS tutorials to the weekend.

## Two tasks next week say they are waiting, and neither really is
- Business Foundations has to be decided on the 30th and is marked as waiting on the SBI loan.
The sanction is now dated 10 November, eleven days after the decision is due. If the fee is what that dependency was about, INSEAD will want your answer long before the money lands, so this is a decision to make on its own rather than one to hold.
- The post-MBA statement on the 31st reads Upcoming and has nothing behind it.
Nothing on the board gates it and nobody else is involved. It is an evening's thinking that then decides your electives, your exchange and when you recruit. - Of everything dated next week, it is the one that gets harder the longer it sits.

## What moved
- You closed the CareerLeader and Career Anchors questionnaires on 18 October.
- You wrote to Campus France New Delhi on the 21st, copying Fitria in Jakarta. That was the one thing the dossier transfer was waiting on.
- INSEAD agreed on the 20th to take the 53,000 euro instalment as a direct bank transfer from your Indian bank.
- The SBI sanction moved to 10 November once it was clear the documents have to be signed at your Indian branch, not in Jakarta.

## What did not
- The board has recorded no change since 19 October. Six days.
- CareerGlobe is dated the 27th and is now the only thing standing between you and booking your first CDC coaching session.
- InCorp's revised quotation has been unanswered since the 12th.
- The four internship applications, the post-MBA statement and the LMS tutorials are all untouched.

## Risks
- The visa is entirely out of your hands and the clock is not. Campus France Delhi has not replied since you wrote on the 21st, and if they are still silent at the end of this week you fly on 4 November with the dossier still in Jakarta. There is nothing to do but chase, which is why it is worth chasing early rather than waiting politely.
- Your first week in India carries almost everything at once. You land on the 4th, your KITAS expires on the 8th, all four applications close on the 8th, and the SBI documents are dated the 10th. Any one of those slipping is survivable; all four landing in the same week in a country you have just moved to is the real exposure.
- The KITAS is the one with no route back. The renewal window closed while the quotation sat, so cancellation is the only option left, and the BPJS claim runs through the same people.
- The money is the one risk that got smaller. With INSEAD taking a direct transfer, the 5 November instalment no longer waits on the loan landing first.

## Put first this week
- One line to InCorp confirming the cancellation. It is the shortest thing on the list and the one with the hardest deadline behind it.
- CareerGlobe, an hour, which unblocks the coaching booking.
- Chase Delhi if nothing has arrived by Tuesday, and copy Fitria again so Jakarta can see you are pushing.

## Today
- The LMS does not open until tonight.
INSEAD says access arrives by end of day, through a new My Courses tab on MyINSEAD. Your tutorials task is dated today, so in practice it is an evening job or tomorrow's. Start with the PLDP tile when it does open, since that is where the mandatory P0 assignments sit.
- The last CV review with a career coach is this afternoon, 13:00 Paris.
It is the non-consulting group, and they ask you to bring the CV in VMock's INSEAD format. Yours has been in the green since 17 October, so the file is ready whether or not you have opened it since. Nothing on the board says you have taken a slot. - If you have not, sign up before this afternoon; there is no later session before the 15 November deadlines.

## Friday
- Business Foundations closes on 30 October, and the money closes with it.
Registration and the 1,530 euro fee both have to be in by then, and INSEAD has now sent its final reminder. Your task still waits on the SBI sanction, which is dated 10 November. - Treat it as a decision on its own; the loan cannot land in time either way.

## Today
- Campus France Jakarta has gone quiet until the middle of November.
Their auto-reply says the office is short-handed through the application season and expects normal service back on 16 November. Jakarta is the end that actually sends your dossier once Delhi confirms, and you land in India on 4 November. - Delhi is the only end still worth pushing.
- INSEAD's visa Ask Me Anything is this evening, 12:00 Paris, 18:00 where you are.
Forty-five minutes, for admits who have not applied yet. Yours is the awkward case - a dossier sitting in Jakarta and an application from Delhi - so it is worth putting to someone who does this every day.

## Still open
- InCorp has had no answer since the 12th, and you fly on the 4th.
Chitra's revised quotation for the cancellation, the tax deregistration and BPJS has been sitting for a fortnight, the renewal window closed while it sat, and the KITAS expires on 8 November. - One line confirming you are cancelling is the whole job.

## You cleared three on Sunday
- The INSEAD CV rebuild, the post-MBA statement and the CareerGlobe profile all went in one evening.
That is the whole of what the career track was waiting on from you, and the CV in particular is what the applications below need in hand.

## The applications are the next real block of work
- Google Strategy and Operations in London, Google Business Analyst in Dublin and Amazon Launch in Luxembourg all close on 8 November.
Each is marked a full day, which puts the start of the last one at 3 November. You fly on the 4th, the KITAS expires on the 8th and the SBI documents are dated the 10th, so that week has no room in it. - Taking a day this week for the first two is the only version of that week that works.

## Today
- Meet Your Class is online this evening, 16:00 Paris, for 45 minutes.
The four in-person admit events are Madrid, Dubai, Toronto and Milan, so this is the only one you can actually get to. Your classmates task has been sitting at the bottom of the board since the start, and an hour online is most of it.

## Tomorrow
- The 1,530 euros for Business Foundations has to be with INSEAD by Friday.
They wrote on Tuesday saying it had not arrived, and they want you to reply to Celine Chin's reminder with the payment proof attached, which is the part most people skip. An international transfer started today may not be credited tomorrow, so the proof is what holds your place while it clears. - Send it this morning if you can, and send the proof the same hour.

## Today
- The 1,530 euros for Business Foundations is due today.
INSEAD wants the transfer with them and the payment proof emailed back to Celine Chin. If the money has gone and the proof has not, the proof is the half still outstanding.

## The visa clock is yours now
- Campus France finished the transfer yesterday and Delhi can see your file.
Nobody else is holding it. INSEAD's immigration officer puts the long-stay visa at seven to eight weeks, and you cannot file until you are in India: filed in your first week there it lands around the end of December, filed a week later the top of that range runs past 3 January. - Book the VFS slot for the days right after you land.

## Before Monday
- Next week carries the flight on the 4th, the KITAS expiry on the 8th and three application deadlines on the 8th.
InCorp has had no answer from you on the cancellation quotation since the 12th and the renewal window has already closed, so the permit lapses by itself unless you tell Chitra otherwise. - One line to her today is the cheapest thing on this list.

## Closed
- You got the Business Foundations payment away on Friday with the receipt attached.
That is the whole task done: registered, paid, proof with their finance team. The module itself is 16 to 20 November, online, which lands in your first full week in India.

## The weekend's one job
- Liesbeth opens her P0 coaching slots on Monday, and she wants the CareerPlan Workbook 48 hours before the session.
You already have the CareerLeader and Career Anchors scores from the middle of the month, so the workbook is transcription rather than work. Book Monday for later that week and it has to be with her by Tuesday. - Wednesday is the flight, so this weekend is when it gets written.
